round1_to_round2.ladder_mean_shift: The 12-month mean ladder fell 1.3-2.5 points in the middle (P>=47 from 0.498 to 0.473, P>=38 from 0.628 to 0.609). The tails barely moved (P>=118 0.075 to 0.074). Implied median moved from about $47 to about $45.7.
round1_to_round2.ladder_1m: All five now use a near-symmetric lognormal with median about $47.0-47.2 and sigma about 0.20. That is almost exactly my round-1 1-month ladder, and the mean differs from it by under 0.01 at every strike.
round1_to_round2.independence_assessment: The convergence is mostly anchoring, not independent agreement. Every agent adopted my round-1 inputs verbatim: 239M FD shares, $336M warrant cash, about $320M capped call, 2027/2028 consensus of $377.7M/$540M, the 'today ~18x / $9.8B EV' framing, the $22-28 contracted value and the 1-month lognormal. With those inputs, my own round-1 primary method ($450M x 19-20x + $1.0B over 239M) already gave about $41; my $44 was set at the top of my range by a $540M x 18x cross-check. The agents applied the same arithmetic with a slightly larger haircut. The only drops that rest on agents' own work are these. Agent_1 and agent_4 cut Materials to a 29% margin, but that figure was also in my round-1 resolution. Agent_3 dropped its 30%-weight $57 sell-side cross-check, as I asked, so its fair value fell even though its fundamental methods rose ($30-36 to $35-37). Agent_4 cited DLA orders, which I checked and which do not support its inference (see disagreements). So the round-2 drop is partly evidence-driven: current consensus, share count, the verified 29% current margin and MP's ramp record. It is also partly over-correction, because a haircut to consensus is stacked on a multiple at or below today's while cash flows roll forward a year. A spread of 36.5-42.5 should not be read as five independent confirmations.

disagreements.topic: Is the fall in fair values to $36.5-42.5 evidence-driven or over-correction?
disagreements.positions: Round-2 fair values: agent_1 $41.0, agent_2 $42.5, agent_3 $36.5, agent_4 $40.0, agent_5 $41.3 (mean $40.3). My round 1 was $44 and the close was $47.29.
disagreements.resolution: Partly evidence-driven, partly over-correction. Evidence-driven parts: 2027 consensus EBITDA was cut ($451.5M to $377.7M). NdPr output is lagging: 2,599t in FY2025, then 917t in Q1-26 and 840t in Q2-26, so Q2 production fell quarter on quarter and is far below the old 6,000t Stage II target. That supports a 10-15% ramp haircut. Over-correction: (a) agent_3's cut comes mainly from removing a sell-side method, not from new fundamentals. (b) A 15-20% haircut combined with a 19-20x NTM multiple at the horizon ignores that 10X's guaranteed EBITDA (at least $140M, escalating) arrives right after the horizon, so NTM to NTM+1 growth at Sep-2027 is still about 30%+. (c) agent_4's competition argument does not hold up. My reconciled fair value is $42.5: NTM at Sep-2027 of about $440M (time-weighted consensus of about $500M less 12%) x 20x = $8.8B, plus about $1.15B of claims, over 239.3M = $41.6. A cross-check at today's 17.4x on $540M plus $1.15B over 239.3M = $44.1. I weight these about 2:1. That is below my round-1 $44 and above the agents' $40.3 mean.
disagreements.evidence: MP Q2-26 8-K (production 840t, sales 1,006t); FY2025 results release (2,599t produced); Q1-26 release (917t); MarketScreener consensus as cited by all agents.

disagreements.topic: agent_1/agent_4: Materials at a ~29% margin at the floor
disagreements.positions: agent_1 puts Materials 2028E at $230M and agent_4 at $200-220M, both scaling Q2's 29% margin roughly linearly. agent_3 uses $260M (38% at scale).
disagreements.resolution: The 29% is correct for Q2: segment adjusted EBITDA of $32.5M on $95.6M revenue plus $17.6M PPA income is 28.7%. It is not a scale margin, though. Q2 sold 1,006t but produced only 840t (inventory drawdown and bill-and-hold), and cash costs of about $80/kg are largely fixed at Mountain Pass, so margins should rise with volume. The bigger risk is volume, not margin: 6,000t by 2028 is optimistic given the output path, and 4,500-5,500t is more defensible. At ~5,000t and $110/kg with a 33-38% margin, Materials earns about $180-210M. The agents' Materials figures are roughly right, but for the wrong reason: the lower volume, not the margin, is what holds them down.
disagreements.evidence: Q2-26 8-K segment tables (Materials revenue $95,629k, PPA $17,580k, segment adjusted EBITDA $32,505k; production 840t, sales 1,006t).

disagreements.topic: agent_4: DLA magnet orders going to competitors as a reason to compress MP's multiple
disagreements.positions: agent_4 holds its multiple at 19x partly because 'DLA magnet-block orders went to E-VAC and Noveon rather than MP'.
disagreements.resolution: Not supported. On 26 May 2026 DLA placed two sole-source maximum $12.9M firm-fixed-price delivery orders, one each to E-VAC (SP8000-26-F-0027) and Noveon (SP8000-26-F-0026). Neither was a competition MP lost. Together they are about $26M of ceiling value, small against MP's ~$450M+ 2026 revenue and its DoW 10X offtake. From 1 Jan 2027, DFARS 252.225-7052 (10 USC 4872) bars defense magnets whose material was mined, refined or separated in covered countries. That probably makes such competitors more likely to need non-China oxide/metal, which MP supplies. Discount the multiple argument; it is worth less than $1/share either way.
disagreements.evidence: DoD contract announcements, 26 May 2026 (GlobalSecurity mirror); DFARS 2027 coverage (Rare Earth Exchanges, Environment+Energy Leader).

disagreements.topic: Net cash and claims at Sep-2027 ($0.95B to $1.32B), and whether I added too much in round 1
disagreements.positions: agent_4 uses $0.95B ($0.95B burn), my round 1 used ~$1.0B (~$0.9B burn), agent_1 $1.21B, agent_5 $1.25B, and agents 2 and 3 $1.32B (~$0.6B burn). agent_3 says I 'assume ~$0.9B burn yet still add ~$1.0B of claims'.
disagreements.resolution: agent_3's critique is wrong as stated. My arithmetic was internally consistent ($1.45B - $0.19B - $0.9B + $0.336B + $0.32B = $1.02B), and agent_3 itself uses more claims ($1.32B). The real disagreement is burn. The 10-Q shows H1-26 operating cash flow of only $4.9M even with $93.3M of PPA cash, H1 capex of $307.7M, a 2026 capex guide of $500-600M net of awards, and 10X capex of over $1.25B weighted to 2027-28. Burn from Jul-2026 to Sep-2027 of about $0.7-0.8B is most likely. That gives claims of about $1.15B (range $1.0-1.3B; capped call about $0.30B in present value). Differences across the agents' range are worth about ±$0.7/share and do not drive the forecast. One thing is new and matters for the left tail: the credit agreement requires at least $500M of unrestricted cash until Consolidated EBITDA reaches $400M or the June-2027 test. With cash heading toward about $0.7B and 10X still being built, a 2027 financing (debt, or possibly equity) is a real in-horizon risk.
disagreements.evidence: Q2-26 10-Q: cash-flow statement, liquidity section (capex guide), Credit Agreement covenant (Covenant Trigger Event, $500.0M minimum unrestricted cash).

disagreements.topic: 2028 / NTM EBITDA base ($400-470M vs $540M consensus) and multiples (18-20x)
disagreements.positions: NTM or 2028E bases: agent_3 $400M at 19x, agent_1 $430M at 20x, agent_5 $430M at 20x, agent_4 $460M at 19x, agent_2 $470M at 18.5x. All describe today's multiple as '~18x / $9.8B EV', taken from my round 1.
disagreements.resolution: Correcting my round-1 figure: today's EV is about $9.4B, not $9.8B. That is 239.3M x $47.29 = $11.32B, less $1.27B of cash net of non-convert debt, less $0.34B warrant cash, less ~$0.30B capped call, which is ~17.4x 2028 consensus. A $430-470M base (a 13-20% haircut to time-weighted consensus of ~$500M) is defensible given the output record, and $400M (agent_3) is the skeptic edge. 18.5-20x on NTM at the horizon is reasonable. The arithmetic has no remaining errors, so this is a judgment band of about $39-44, not a factual dispute.
disagreements.evidence: 10-Q balance sheet and capital-structure notes; MarketScreener consensus.

disagreements.topic: Thesis break $28-30 and the contracted/floor value
disagreements.positions: agents 1 and 3 use $28, agent_2 $29, agents 4 and 5 $30. All five cite my round-1 contracted value of '$22-28/share'.
disagreements.resolution: My $22-28 was too high. Floor-protected Materials ($130-200M x ~12-15x = $1.6-3.0B), plus a 10X guarantee NPV of $0.6-1.0B, plus today's claims of ~$1.9B, comes to $4.1-5.9B, or about $17-25/share on 239.3M. So at a $29 break the market would still be paying about $4-12/share for Independence magnets, HREE and the policy option. That is close enough to 'nothing for the growth story' to serve as a thesis break. I keep $29, the agents' mean, but the agents that trimmed the deep left tail citing $22-28 as support leaned on an overstated floor.
disagreements.evidence: Recalculation from 10-Q terms (PPA $110/kg, 10X $140M guarantee, capital structure).

disagreements.topic: In-horizon policy catalysts: the 10 Jan 2027 truce expiry and the 1 Jan 2027 DoD China-magnet rule
disagreements.positions: All five treat 10 Jan 2027 as the main two-sided policy event. agents 4 and 5 add the 1 Jan 2027 DFARS change as a '+' catalyst. agent_2 adds APEC Shenzhen (Nov 2026).
disagreements.resolution: Both dates are correct and inside the horizon. The truce extension to 10 Jan 2027 was confirmed in round 1. The DFARS 252.225-7052 scope widens from 'melted or produced' to 'mined, refined, separated, melted, or produced' on 1 Jan 2027, with waivers still possible. The DFARS change is long scheduled and structural, so it should support demand and offtakes rather than move the price on the day. The 10 Jan cliff is the real binary, and it justifies keeping both 12-month tails at the agents' mean. No new 8-K through 1 Oct, so Q3 results remain ~Nov 5, outside the 1-month window.
disagreements.evidence: CNBC 2026-09-24; Rinnovabili 2026-09-25; DFARS 2027 coverage; EDGAR submissions (latest filing a 30 Sep Form 4, no 8-K).

revision_check.note: It checked the capped call and the EDGAR date itself and dropped the stale CFRA method, which were the right fixes. Its 'own' finding of a 29% Materials margin is my round-1 number, scaled linearly, and that understates operating leverage. The new SOTP of $31.8 at 20% weight drags the blend. Thesis break $28 rests on my overstated $22-28 floor.

It re-fetched MarketScreener and NdPr prices and corrected the share count. Its methods are internally consistent. It did only 2 new queries, and its industry lane added little that is new (Lynas derating and Western entrants, as in round 1). Its $1.32B claims assume burn on the low side.

It correctly fixed the convert count and raised its fundamental base, which raised its fundamental values. Its lower blend comes from deleting the $57 sell-side method, not from a new bearish fact. Its critique of my claims arithmetic is wrong (my numbers add up; the real difference is burn), and it then uses larger claims than I did. The 20% haircut is a defensible skeptic edge, but the low fair value is not evidence of new downside.

It made a real improvement in lane quality: SMM weekly prices, China customs magnet exports (-18% YoY, US -21% MoM in August) and DoD contract notices. But it misread the DLA notices: two sole-source $12.9M max orders are not lost competitions and do not justify a lower multiple. It also uses the heaviest burn ($0.95B claims).

It accepted the corrections and re-verified consensus. Its base-rate distribution (median +4%, 10th percentile -47%, 90th +205% over 63 windows) is still its independent contribution and justifies keeping the median near spot even though fair value is lower. Its P/E method at 45x on a haircut EPS largely repeats its EV/EBITDA result, so it is not a separate check.

one_month_reasoning: No scheduled catalyst falls in 1-30 Oct: EDGAR shows no 8-K setting a Q3 date (latest filing a 30 Sep Form 4), Q3 has come Nov 2-7 every year since 2021, and the China truce runs to 10 Jan 2027. In-window news is limited to China's post-Golden-Week SMM prices, September customs magnet data (~Oct 20) and headlines. So I keep the agents' mean ladder: a near-symmetric lognormal, median ~$47.1, monthly sigma ~0.20.
confidence_reason: The round-2 forecasts converged mainly by adopting my round-1 inputs. My searches settled several smaller points: the DLA orders, the claims arithmetic, the covenant, the 29% margin's context and the contracted value. They support only a slight upward nudge (+0.5 to +0.9 points) in the middle of the ladder against a 74%-volatility stock. None overturns the mean.
thesis_break_reason: At $29 the ~239M-share equity is about $6.9B. Corrected contracted value (Materials at the $110 floor, 10X guarantee NPV and today's ~$1.9B of claims) is only about $17-25/share, so at $29 the market would be paying just $4-12/share for Independence magnets, HREE and the policy option. A sustained trade there most likely means failed GM qualification, a 10X funding gap or equity raise (the $500M minimum-cash covenant runs to the June-2027 test), weaker DoW support, or a durable China deal after 10 Jan 2027, not ordinary volatility.
key_drivers: The 10 Jan 2027 expiry of China's suspended export controls is the main two-sided binary. The 1 Jan 2027 DFARS mine-to-magnet rule is a structural support, not a dated price event.

The ramp is behind: NdPr output was 2,599t in FY2025, then 917t in Q1-26 and 840t in Q2-26, while the 2027 consensus EBITDA of $377.7M requires about 3x the ~$114M run rate. Most current EBITDA is PPA income (62% in Q2).

Capital structure: ~239M FD shares, ~$1.15B of net claims at Sep-2027, and heavy 10X capex against a $500M minimum-cash covenant until EBITDA reaches $400M or the June-2027 test, which raises the risk of a 2027 financing.
Valuation: EV ~$9.4B is ~17.4x 2028 consensus ($540M). Reconciled fair value is $42.5 against a $47.29 close, so the price carries a policy and scarcity premium of about $5.
Two-way flow: 23% short interest, CEO sales of ~$78M at $64-71 earlier in 2026, and a sell-side mean (~$74-76) that lags and is being cut.

fair_value.reason: NTM EBITDA at Sep-2027 of ~$440M (time-weighted 2027/2028 consensus of ~$500M less 12% for the ramp record) x 20x = $8.8B, plus ~$1.15B of claims at Sep-2027 (cash $1.45B less $0.19B non-convert debt, less ~$0.75B burn, plus $0.336B warrant cash, plus ~$0.30B capped call), over 239.3M FD shares = $41.6. The market-multiple cross-check (17.4x today on $540M 2028 consensus, plus $1.15B) = $44.1. Weighted about 2:1, this gives $42.5. It is above the agents' $40.3 mean because agent_3's drop comes from removing a method rather than from new evidence, and agent_4's competition discount fails a check. It is below my round-1 $44, which sat at the top of my own range and used an overstated $9.8B / 18x current EV.

The $500M minimum-cash covenant applies only until Consolidated EBITDA reaches $400M or the June-2027 test (10-Q Credit Agreement note), not indefinitely.
My round-1 $22-28 contracted value was too high; it is ~$17-25. Your $28 break and trimmed left tail lean on it.

summary: In round 2 the five fair values fell to $36.5-42.5 (mean $40.3), and the ladders moved about 2 points lower in the middle. The convergence is largely the agents adopting my round-1 inputs rather than independent agreement. Fact-checks show the drop is partly real: the ramp is lagging (Q2 output 840t, below Q1) and consensus has been cut. It is also partly over-correction: agent_3 deleted a method, agent_4's DLA 'lost orders' were two small sole-source awards to others, and my own round-1 contracted value ($22-28) and current EV ($9.8B) were too high. I reconcile fair value at $42.5, keep the thesis break at $29 and nudge the middle of the ladder up under a point. The 10 Jan 2027 China cliff and a possible 2027 financing (a $500M minimum-cash covenant against heavy 10X capex) are the in-horizon events that matter.
